li.a: US Department of Justice: Justice Department charges light rail attacker with federal crime
CBS News: DOJ charges man for deadly stabbing of Ukrainian refugee Iryna Zarutska in North Carolina
ABC7: Ukrainian refugee stabbed to death on NC train in Charlotte, suspect facing federal charge, DOJ says
WBTV: Grand jury indicts man accused of killing Ukrainian woman on Charlotte light rail
WBTV: Defense requests federal competency hearing for man accused of killing Iryna Zarutska
CNN: Charlotte train stabbing federal case delayed over suspect's mental competency
WBTV: Court transcript shows accused Charlotte light rail stabber spoke out during federal competency hearing
WBTV: "Systemic failures", Zarutska family sues Charlotte and security contractor one year after light rail death

content.p: Iryna Zarutska, a 23-year-old Ukrainian refugee, was stabbed to death on a light-rail train in Charlotte, North Carolina, on the night of 22 August 2025. She had been sitting in front of a man she did not know, and she was attacked from behind within minutes of boarding. Decarlos Brown Jr., 34, was arrested on the platform a short time later and has been charged under both state and federal law.

Brown has not been tried. He is accused, and he is presumed innocent. A state psychiatric facility and then a federal judge found him unable to stand trial for now, and he was sent for treatment in June 2026. His lawyers describe a long history of severe mental illness. Surveillance video of the attack, which went viral after its release in September 2025, brought the case national attention and comment from politicians across the country.

According to ABC7, Zarutska had left Ukraine's war behind and settled in Charlotte with her mother, sister and brother. CNN reported that she fled in 2022, had a degree in art and restoration, worked at a pizzeria, and was studying to become a veterinary assistant. Her obituary, quoted by ABC7, said many remembered seeing her walking neighbours' pets through the neighbourhood and that she dreamed of becoming a veterinary assistant. People who knew her described a gifted artist who sculpted and designed clothes.

According to WBTV, she entered the train at 9:46 p.m. on 22 August and sat in front of Brown. ABC7 reported, citing WSOC, that she was wearing headphones and that the two had no interaction. An FBI affidavit, summarised by the Justice Department, says that about four minutes later Brown took a knife from his pocket and struck her three times from behind. Police responded to a call at about 9:55 p.m. and found her fatally wounded. CBS, describing the same affidavit, wrote that police found one wound at the centre of her neck and a minor cut on her left knee.

At least one bystander ran to help at 9:52 p.m., WBTV said, and about 30 seconds later Brown got off at the next stop. Officers arrested him on the platform. He was treated at a hospital for a cut to his hand before being charged with murder, WBTV reported, and it was unclear how he had been injured. Investigators say the two did not know each other, and a motive was not immediately clear.

CBS, citing The Associated Press, reported that Brown had a long criminal record, among it a five-year prison term for armed robbery, and had been diagnosed with schizophrenia. His mother told a local television station that she had lately tried to have him committed to psychiatric care against his will, after violence at home. His sister told CNN that he "didn't seem like himself" after prison. WBTV reported that in January 2025 he was arrested for misuse of 911 and police officers wrote that he believed someone had given him a "man-made" material that controlled when he ate, walked and talked.

The Charlotte Area Transit System released the surveillance video, and Mayor Vi Lyles thanked media outlets and residents who chose not to repost it out of respect for the family, ABC7 reported. She said more officers would be assigned to patrol the rail system. The transit agency banned Brown for life. WBTV Investigates later reported that Brown had boarded a city bus hours before the stabbing and then rode the light rail for more than an hour without his fare being checked or anyone questioning him. Ferguson told reporters that after Zarutska's death the embassy in Ukraine called to offer to help bring her home, and that her family said no because she loved America and they would bury her in the United States.

Brown was charged with first-degree murder in state court and ordered to stay in jail and undergo an evaluation. On 9 September 2025, after the video went viral, the Justice Department filed a federal complaint with a single count: causing a death on a mass transportation system. Attorney General Pamela Bondi said she had directed her lawyers to prosecute him federally and "will seek the maximum penalty", and the maximum is life in prison or death. US Attorney Russ Ferguson said the surveillance video gave prosecutors the basis for the federal charge and that he had begun to think of the federal option when he saw people afraid to ride the light rail.

On 22 October 2025 a grand jury indicted him on the federal count, which WBTV described as violence against a railroad carrier and mass transit system leading to death. WBTV reported that the indictment says he could be eligible for the death penalty on the basis of a 2015 armed robbery conviction. WBTV reported that Brown has been in federal custody since October 2025 and that the federal case takes priority over the state's. A lawyer for the Zarutska family said the family was pleased with the indictment and hopeful of swift justice.

A state psychiatric facility deemed Brown "incapable to proceed" in the state case earlier in 2026, WBTV reported, but a judge still has to rule formally. On 7 May his federal public defenders asked for a competency hearing, writing that "for years, Decarlos Brown has suffered from debilitating mental illness and impairment, including severe delusions" and that he believes a man-made material is controlling his movements. Prosecutors supported the hearing. The Federal Bureau of Prisons examined him and found him currently incompetent, with a good prognosis for restoration through treatment. The US Attorney's memorandum noted that competency to stand trial is a separate matter from an insanity defence.

On 9 June 2026 Judge Kenneth Bell found Brown not competent "at this time" and committed him to the custody of the attorney general for treatment at a secure federal medical facility for no more than four months. Another hearing would be needed if forced medication was thought necessary. Brown shouted several times in court. According to a transcript unsealed months later, he said the FBI refused to investigate and he wanted to press charges, including against the judge. Ferguson said Brown was not being released and he hoped he would stand trial. The state case has been delayed at least six months, and state prosecutors have said they will wait until the federal case is over.

President Donald Trump and other administration officials used the killing to criticise Democratic-led cities, CNN reported. White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt called her death "entirely preventable". North Carolina's legislature passed "Iryna's Law", signed on 3 October 2025, which includes restoring the death penalty in the state. Governor Josh Stein objected to the return of executions and to a firing-squad option, calling the action "barbaric".

On 21 August 2026 the Zarutska family sued the city of Charlotte and Professional Security Services, the private security contractor for the Charlotte Area Transit System, alleging negligence. Their attorney, Lauren Newton, said the suit points to a lack of physical barriers, no fare enforcement and an under-staffed armed security force: it alleges the contract budgeted 219 security positions including 39 armed, but that the contractor had 183 staff and 11 armed guards on the day of the attack. The suit cites four homicides near Blue Line stops in recent years to argue that violence was foreseeable. Many of these issues also appeared in a report by the state auditor, Dave Boliek, WBTV said. The city said it does not comment on active litigation and the contractor had not responded.
